abstract: The ability of epidermal growth factor (EGF) to modulate the secretion of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in both normal and malignant placental cells was compared. Receptors for EGF were present on the JAr line of choriocarcinoma cells and were localized to the trophoblast cells of normal placental organ cultures as detected by immunofluorescence. Despite the presence of EGF receptors, the normal placenta did not respond to EGF by significantly increasing its levels of hCG production. The JAr line of choriocarcinoma exhibited a 2-fold increase in hCG secretion after the addition of EGF. EGF stimulated growth in the JAr cells, as measured by the protein content of the cultures, but did not elevate the incorporation of [methyl-3H]thymidine in either the JAr cells or placental organ cultures.
abstract_ja: 上皮成長因子(EGF)が正常および悪性胎盤細胞におけるヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)分泌を調節する能力を比較した。EGF受容体は絨毛癌細胞株JArに存在し、免疫蛍光法で正常胎盤器官培養の栄養膜細胞に局在していた。EGF受容体が存在するにもかかわらず、正常胎盤はEGFに対してhCG産生を有意に増加させなかった。絨毛癌株JArはEGF添加後にhCG分泌が2倍に増加した。EGFはJAr細胞の培養液中のタンパク質量で測定される増殖を促進したが、JAr細胞および胎盤器官培養のいずれにおいても[メチル-3H]チミジンの取り込みは増加させなかった。
